label: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017
output:
To: timeline
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: none

Spent the last two Saturdays rewiring a buddy’s shed. I’m putting this up partly so I remember it, and partly so somebody reads it before they let their cousin’s neighbor “just hook it up” because he watched a video.

This was not a close call. This was a countdown.

What I found, in no particular order:

- Power was three orange extension cords daisy-chained out the basement window, across the yard, and under the deck. Three. Daisy-chained. Outside. In weather.
- One splice was wrapped in duct tape. Not electrical tape. Duct tape. I want to be clear about that.
- A 30 amp breaker feeding 14 gauge wire. That’s not a circuit, that’s a fire waiting for a calendar date.
- The shed outlet was hooked up with speaker wire. Speaker wire. For a building. With a roof.
- The “GFCI” was a regular outlet with a GFCI sticker stuck on it. The sticker was doing all the safety work.
- The ceiling fan box was held up by one drywall screw. One. And not a good one.
- Mouse nest in the junction box. Mice were fine. Unbothered. Probably had better wiring than the shed.
- Inside the panel door, in Sharpie: “SHED - DONT TOUCH - RON.”

So I open the panel, and my wife is standing there, and she goes, “Who’s Ron?” Like I’m supposed to know. Like Ron is on my Christmas card list. I don’t know Ron. Ron is a ghost who does electrical work for pizza.

And here’s the thing: I don’t think Ron was evil. Cheap and a little proud. That’s most of these. Somebody’s buddy did it for a case of beer, it worked for eight years, and now it’s everybody’s problem. I’ve seen it a hundred times. It’s always fine until it isn’t, and then it’s not a funny story anymore.

This is how houses burn down. Not usually from some big dramatic thing. From a splice in the wrong tape, a breaker that’s too big for the wire, a fan box hanging by one screw, and somebody saying, “It’s been fine.” Fine is not a rating.

The fix was not fancy: trenched 18 inches, 12/2 UF, 20 amp GFCI breaker, real boxes, real outlets, fan on a proper brace. Done. Safe. Boring. That’s what you want with electrical.

If your shed, garage, basement, or “man cave” has any of this going on, please stop using it and call a licensed electrician. Not your buddy with a YouTube video and a roll of duct tape. Not the guy who says he’s done it before. An actual licensed guy. Pull a permit, get it looked at. It’s cheaper than a new house and a lot cheaper than being the reason somebody gets hurt.

I got paid in two pizzas and a case of Yuengling, which is honestly the best-paying job I’ve had in a while. The fan works. Nothing smells like burning. That’s the goal.

And Ron, wherever you are: I hope your extension cords are at least indoors now.

reasons: The draft reveals the private message’s detail that nothing smells like burning.
